frequency_question: What proportion of major bills requiring standard committee referral, markup, floor scheduling, debate, and roll-call votes can complete the physical procedural timeline within 321 days?
membership_rule: Includes any primary legislative bill that underwent standard committee processing and floor passage in the U.S. Senate; excludes purely procedural resolutions, conference reports without original chamber text processing, and omnibus packages bypassing standard committee stages.
provenance_note: 8 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: Sample of prominent major bills meeting the structural criteria across multiple congressional sessions.
known_gaps: Does not account for non-prioritized bills that languish indefinitely due to low legislative priority (though forbidden from considering motivation/opposition, pure calendar capacity allows it if prioritized).
skeleton: Legislative process timelines: Committee referral (30 days) + Hearings/Markup (45 days) + Floor Scheduling/Cloture (30 days) + Debate/Amendments (15 days) + Final Vote (1 day) = 121 baseline days, well within the 321-day window.
multiplier: 8 hits out of 10 sampled major contested statutory bills that successfully completed the procedural pipeline within a sub-year timeframe when prioritized.
validity_reason: Senate standing rules regarding cloture and committee pacing have remained stable across decades.
